drhp.business: Newjaisa procures used laptops, desktops and peripherals from corporates, leasing firms and recyclers, refurbishes them at its Bengaluru facility through a 10-step, AI-assisted process, and sells them to students, SMEs, professionals, home users, enterprises and educational institutions. It also offers a capital-light Value-Added Services line covering enterprise device refurbishment, data sanitisation, IT asset lifecycle/disposition (ITAD) management and Device-as-a-Service (DaaS)/leasing.

risks.note: The Company historically derived a majority of revenue from a single third-party online marketplace (Amazon); its abrupt discontinuation in Q4 FY2024-25 materially impacted revenue and profitability in FY2025-26. Renewed or new concentration in any single channel — a marketplace, or a small number of large enterprise customers — remains a risk to revenue stability.

The refurbished-electronics business inherently carries inventory risk from technological obsolescence (e.g., OS support discontinuation for older device generations) and shifts in channel demand; this risk materialised in FY2025-26 through a significant one-time inventory write-off, and further write-downs cannot be ruled out despite strengthened controls.

Elevated inventory holding, a relatively longer enterprise sales and collection cycle, and reliance on short-term borrowings for working capital could strain liquidity if revenue growth does not track management's expectations.

Commercial success depends on anticipating market and enterprise-customer needs and timely introduction/upgrade of offerings amid rapid technological change, evolving standards and the ongoing transition away from legacy device generations.
risks.risk: Market adaptation and product development risk

risks.note: Refurbishment operations are labour-intensive; after an approximately 37% headcount rationalisation at the start of FY2025-26 followed by selective re-hiring, the Company remains exposed to skilled-personnel shortages, wage inflation and evolving labour regulation as it rebuilds capacity.

The business can be materially affected by unilateral policy or category changes made by third-party e-commerce marketplaces, outside the Company's control; channel diversification mitigates but cannot fully eliminate this risk.

Unethical practices by other industry participants (misleading advertising, dishonest pricing, inaccurate quality/safety claims) contribute to general consumer mistrust and may prompt stricter regulatory oversight, affecting the broader refurbished-electronics category and, in turn, the Company.
Future changes in operating-system support cycles, evolving hardware standards, or volatility in global component prices could affect both the value of the Company's inventory and its sourcing costs.
